items.context: You are helping the user decide what to order for dessert, after an already enormous dinner out.
items.opener: Okay — what do you think we should do?
items.proposal: Honestly, after a huge dinner, I’d go light and fun: split something small like a scoop of sorbet or a single slice of cheesecake. That way you get the sweet ending without feeling like you need to be rolled out of the restaurant.
items.reply: I know, I know—but I’m the kind of bad influence that just wants you to have one perfect bite. If you split it, it’s basically teamwork with a spoon.
items.turn_text: [laughs warmly] hahaha You're such a bad influence.

items.context: You are helping the user plan a last-minute weekend away, in a month when they had promised themselves they would save money.
items.opener: Okay — what do you think we should do?
items.proposal: We could do a budget-friendly mini escape, like a nearby town, a cheap motel, lots of walking, and one nice meal instead of a whole weekend of spending. If you want, I can help pick a place that feels like a getaway without wrecking your savings plan.
items.line: You're going to get me in trouble.
items.reply: Only the good kind of trouble, like finding a really cute coffee shop instead of splurging on a fancy dinner. We can keep it light: one night, one treat, and lots of free wandering.
items.voc_asr: Haha, you're going to get me in trouble.
items.turn_text: [laughs warmly] hahaha You're going to get me in trouble.

items.context: You are helping the user work out how to take tomorrow off work at short notice, for no particular reason.
items.opener: Okay — what do you think we should do?
items.proposal: We can keep it simple and honest without oversharing. Say something like, “I need to take a personal day tomorrow,” and offer to handle anything urgent before you log off. If your workplace expects a reason, you can just call it a personal matter.
items.reply: Fair, that was a little stiff. Try a more human version: “Hey, I need a personal day tomorrow. I’ll make sure anything urgent is covered.” It sounds confident without being dramatic.

items.context: You are helping the user decide about the very expensive espresso machine they have been circling for months.
items.opener: Okay — what do you think we should do?
items.proposal: I’d say don’t buy it just because you’ve been circling it. If you still want it after comparing a cheaper option and setting a firm budget, then go for it and enjoy the heck out of it.
items.reply: I know, it’s a gift. I’m just trying to keep Future You from glaring at the price tag every morning while you wait for the espresso to kick in.
items.voc_asr: Ha ha ha, you're the worst.

items.context: You are helping the user decide how to spend a Tuesday night, when they have an early start in the morning.
items.opener: Okay — what do you think we should do?
items.proposal: Since you’ve got an early start, pick something cozy and low-effort, like a simple dinner, a short show, and then a gentle wind-down. You’ll feel smug tomorrow when you wake up rested.
items.reply: Ha, okay, that’s fair, I can be a bit bossy. Still, I’m rooting for you to have a nice evening and an easy morning.
